name: Queen conch
summary: Seasonally closed and subject to shell-size, landing, trip-limit, and water-specific rules.
sizeRules: Minimum 9-inch shell length from spire to distal end, or 3/8-inch lip thickness.
notes: Territorial commercial trip limit: 150 per registered vessel with a licensed commercial fisher present.
Federal harvest is addressed for St. Croix; the handbook says no queen conch harvest or possession in the St. Thomas/St. John EEZ.
Must be landed alive, whole, and in shell under the summarized territorial rules.

name: West Indian topsnail (whelk)
summary: Territorial harvest is seasonally closed and subject to a minimum shell diameter.
sizeRules: Minimum shell diameter greater than 2 7/16 inches at the widest point.
notes: Must be landed live and whole in the shell.

name: Caribbean spiny lobster
summary: Minimum carapace size applies; egg-bearing females and puncturing gear are prohibited.
notes: Must be landed whole; egg-bearing females may not be harvested.
Spears, hooks, similar puncturing devices, gillnets, and trammel nets may not be used to take lobster.

name: Other listed parrotfishes
summary: Queen, princess, striped, redtail, stoplight, yellowtail, and redband parrotfish have water- and district-specific size summaries.
sizeRules: St. Croix federal waters: 9-inch fork length for listed allowable parrotfishes.
St. Croix federal waters: redband parrotfish minimum 8-inch fork length.
The handbook summarizes no federal minimum size for St. Thomas/St. John parrotfishes.
notes: Species identification must be certain before applying a rule.

name: Tarpon
summary: Catch-and-release using hook and line only under the summarized territorial rule.
notes: No harvest; hook-and-line catch and release only.

notes: No harvest; hook-and-line catch and release only.

name: Sea turtles and eggs
summary: No harvest, possession, or harassment.
notes: Applies to all sea turtle species and their eggs.

name: Corals, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers
summary: Federal fishing or possession prohibition summarized for these groups.
notes: Incidental take must be returned immediately in the general area of fishing under the summarized federal rule.

name: Southern pink shrimp
summary: Special St. Croix lagoon rules and a recreational permit requirement apply.
notes: No commercial harvest or sale in Altona Lagoon or Great Pond.
Recreational harvest requires a permit; the handbook lists a $10 annual fee.
Sale is prohibited, and gear/location restrictions apply.

name: Tunas, billfish, swordfish, and sharks
summary: Permit, retention, reporting, landing, and in-season federal rules vary by species and activity.
notes: Do not infer a current retention or size limit from this handbook; use current NOAA HMS guidance.
Some recreational landings and discards require reporting within 24 hours.
